title: What was Jesus like as a boy?
text: The Bible tells us only a little about Jesus as a boy. He grew up in Nazareth with St. Mary and St. Joseph, and He obeyed them. When Jesus was twelve, the family went to Jerusalem for the feast of Passover. On the way home, Mary and Joseph could not find Him. After three days they found Him in the Temple, sitting with the teachers, listening to them and asking questions. Everyone was amazed at how well He understood. Jesus told His mother that He must be in His Father's house. Then He went home with them and obeyed them. The Bible says that Jesus grew in wisdom and in size, and people and God were pleased with Him.

title: Does God love me?
text: Yes! God loves you very much, and He loves you just as you are. The Bible tells us that God is love. He loved us so much that He sent His Son, Jesus, to save us. God loves you when you are happy and when you are sad. He loves you even when you make a mistake, and He is always ready to forgive you when you say sorry. You never have to do anything special to make God love you. His love for you never ends. When we remember how much God loves us, we want to love Him back and to love other people too.

title: What are the Psalms?
text: The Psalms are 150 songs and prayers in the Bible. Many of them were written by King David, who played the harp and sang to God while he took care of his sheep. Some Psalms say thank you to God, some ask for help, and some praise Him with joy. We pray the Psalms in church and in the Agpeya, the book of daily prayers, and we sing them in our hymns. When you are happy, sad or afraid, you can pray a Psalm too. Psalm 23, The Lord is my shepherd, is a favorite of many children.

title: What is the Creed?
text: The Creed is a short prayer that tells what we believe. We say it together in the Holy Liturgy. It starts with the words, We believe in one God, God the Father, the Almighty, Creator of heaven and earth. It tells us that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, that He was born of the Virgin Mary, died on the cross, rose again on the third day and went up to heaven. It speaks about the Holy Spirit, the Giver of life, about one holy Church, about baptism, and about the life of the world to come. The bishops first wrote the Creed at the Council of Nicaea, where St. Athanasius of Alexandria defended the faith that Jesus is truly God.

title: What is the Book of Acts?
text: The Book of Acts tells what happened after Jesus went up to heaven. St. Luke wrote it, the same Luke who wrote the Gospel of Luke. It tells how the Holy Spirit came on the apostles at Pentecost, and how the Church began in Jerusalem and then grew in many countries. You can read about St. Peter, St. Stephen and the journeys of St. Paul, who told people everywhere about Jesus. The book shows us that the Church is a family that prays together, shares and helps each other.

title: What is the Sermon on the Mount?
text: One day Jesus went up on a mountainside, and a big crowd came to listen. He sat down and taught them many things. We call this the Sermon on the Mount. Jesus began with the Beatitudes, which tell who God blesses: people who are gentle, who are sorry for their sins, who are merciful, who have pure hearts and who make peace. He taught us to love our enemies, to pray, to forgive, and to trust God who takes care of the birds and the flowers. He also gave us the golden rule: treat other people the way you want them to treat you. In this teaching Jesus also taught the Lord's Prayer.

title: Is it okay to feel sad?
text: Yes, it is okay to feel sad sometimes. Everyone feels sad, and even Jesus cried when His friend Lazarus died. God is very close to us when we are sad. You can tell Jesus how you feel in a prayer, using your own words. It also helps to talk to someone you trust, like your mom, dad, servant or Abouna. They love you and want to listen. Feeling sad does not last forever. God gives comfort and joy again, and He is always with you.
